headline: PDE authors prove conditional regularity for an axisymmetric Navier–Stokes blowup profile with analytic forcing
summary: Peter Constantin, Mihaela Ignatova and Vlad Vicol report a theorem for suitable weak solutions of forced 3D Navier–Stokes: if the force is bounded in C² up to the proposed singular time and spatially real analytic locally before it, while the angular mean obeys specified anisotropic Type II estimates and the full solution is exactly axisymmetric on a shrinking core at every pre-singular time, then the solution is regular at the point. Their arXiv v2 appendix derives two velocity hypotheses from statements in OpenAI’s proposed construction and conditionally concludes that a force in that construction cannot vanish identically near the singular point or be locally spatially analytic under the stated bound. The paper expressly says it does not verify the OpenAI construction. OpenAI’s described compactly supported smooth residual force is nonanalytic, so the theorem constrains a force class and does not refute the proposed construction or resolve the Clay problem.
